planted_anomaly_detections.note: The frozen budget (37 orphaned INVOICE_LINE rows, 50 unparseable SIGNUP_DT values, 31 malformed RELATED_ACCT_IDS lists) sits in other units. USAGE_EVENTS, RATING_PERIODS and RATING_RESULTS carry none of it, so the expected set for U4-usage is empty and nothing extra turned up.

unverified_paths: Live mode reads the locally seeded copy of the estate (seed 714559852, namespace demo), not the parent's container. The data is byte-identical by construction, but no query ran against the parent's instance.

The harness has no rule for yn_to_bool, csv_split_trim or parse_date_string and cannot compare an integer code against its decoded string. kind is therefore graded by tier 4 recorded operations, not by a field-level rule.

The $jsonSchema validator on usage_events is asserted by reading it back from Atlas and replayed logically by the usage_validator_domain operation; no rejected write was attempted, so its enforcement behaviour is untested.
Every source row satisfies the validator today (units > 0, kind in api|storage|compute), so the dirty-value path (null plus legacy.<field>Raw) never executes in this unit.
PKG_RATING's TO_CHAR(...,'YYYYMMDD') date comparison is a source quirk and is deliberately not reproduced; no test covers callers that depend on it.
The pre-PR self-check asks for an ow_tp / ow-tp- namespace prefix. This batch's contract names ow_billing_migration, so that prefix rule is not met by design.
M0 scale: index choice is graded for correctness, not for performance at production volume.

tier4_operations.why: Each records a source_sql and a target_pipeline so the decoded CODES value and the PKG_RATING roll-up are graded on both stacks.
